comment: Defaults only - every number here can be overridden per installation from the GUI.
The error-rate figures are anchored to a real fault and a real clean link measured on the
reference machine: a fibre link with mismatched transceivers ran at 38,100 ppm (3.81% of
received frames failing CRC) while the port beside it, on the same chip, measured 0 ppm over
700,000 frames. 'fail' therefore sits an order of magnitude below the observed fault and two
orders above the observed noise floor.
min_frames exists because a rate computed from a handful of frames is not a measurement. Below
it the verdict is 'idle' - neither green nor red - and the GUI says so in words.

max_accumulate_seconds: a quiet port keeps adding its windows together until it has min_frames to judge, or until this long has passed - after which it is judged on what little it saw, and says so. Without this a lightly used gigabit port would read 'not enough traffic' for ever, which is how the owner noticed the gap.

duplex_ppm.comment: Collisions on a link that negotiated full duplex mean a duplex mismatch, which is a fault at any rate, so the bar is much lower than for receive errors.

flaps.comment: A single cable reseat produced five kernel events inside one second on the reference machine, so events closer together than debounce_seconds count as one.

comment: Receive power ranges are the IEEE 802.3 figures for the media type: minimum is the receiver
sensitivity, maximum the overload point. The module's own DDM thresholds are read where
available but are clamped to these, because vendors set them far looser - one module on the
reference machine declares its low-power alarm 6.2 dB below the specification floor.
These produce advisory reasons only. They never decide a verdict on their own: throughout a
genuine 3.81% CRC fault, both modules read fully inside every one of their own limits.

margin_db.comment: How close to the limit still deserves a mention. Inside this band of the minimum receive power the port is reported as 'optical margin is thin' rather than as a fault.

load_test.comment: payload is used when the interface MTU allows a jumbo frame, payload_small otherwise. The test saturates the link while it runs, which is why it is never automatic.
